historical_reviews.deepseek: Mistakes an OS-visible functional SSIF test for a physical-only activity.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Recognizes the path-attribution gap but resolves it with unsupported probing instead of transport/driver evidence.
historical_reviews.related_cases: This row is specifically FPGA-to-BMC I2C-1 SSIF; generic BMC reachability through KCS, BT, LAN or another `/dev/ipmi` interface does not satisfy it.

original_test_intent: Verify a functional host-to-BMC SSIF exchange over the named FPGA and BMC I2C-1 path by obtaining valid BMC information through the correct local IPMI transport without fallback to another interface.
original_method: Identify the FPGA, BMC I2C-1 and OS IPMI device/driver mapping; disable or account for alternate transport selection; capture driver/interface and error baseline; run the source read-only BMC-info request through the approved local SSIF interface; validate exit status and required identity fields; correlate SSIF/I2C/FPGA counters/logs and confirm no fallback or new errors.
manual_activity: Platform/BMC owner supplies the authoritative FPGA-to-I2C-1 SSIF mapping and approved local interface selection; no board probing is required unless separately scoped.
required_inputs: Platform diagram mapping host IPMI device through FPGA to BMC I2C-1 SSIF
OS driver/module and `/dev/ipmi*` or equivalent interface corresponding to that SSIF path
Approved `ipmitool` build/interface option and sudo policy
Expected BMC Device ID, Device Revision, Firmware Revision, IPMI Version and manufacturer/product identity fields
Method to prove no KCS/BT/LAN/alternate-interface fallback
SSIF/I2C/FPGA error counters or logs, timeout and retry acceptance limits
safety_requirements: Use only read-only BMC information requests
Confirm selected local interface and privilege scope before sudo
Do not unload drivers, alter SSIF/I2C routing, reset BMC or probe hardware for this static functional run
Bound command timeout and capture failure once without automatic retry masking an intermittent link
Preserve existing logs and compare transport-specific error deltas
agent_execution_scope: Collect OS/BMC/FPGA identity, driver/interface mapping and read-only error baseline
After owner confirmation, run the exact bounded local BMC-info command and correlate SSIF evidence
Do not choose transport by default behavior, probe/solder, mutate management state, retry automatically or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve the named SSIF interface and FPGA/I2C-1 mapping
Define expected response fields, timeout/retry and no-fallback evidence
Review command plus transport evidence and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incorrect: the source's OS command is remotely executable and read-only; physical probing is not stated.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain `sudo ipmitool bmc info` only after proving the default local interface is the named SSIF path; otherwise specify the owner-approved local interface explicitly. Capture complete stdout/stderr, exit code, duration and SSIF/FPGA/I2C error deltas.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: OS execution, `sudo ipmitool bmc info`, FPGA, BMC I2C-1, Common branch and 15/5-minute scope are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute one bounded read-only IPMI BMC-info transaction through a proven FPGA/I2C-1 SSIF interface and correlate driver/transport telemetry.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds path attribution, expected response fields and no-fallback/error evidence while removing invented physical probing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful generic ipmitool response proves BMC reachability only; without interface mapping it may traverse KCS, BT, LAN or a different IPMI device and miss the named SSIF path.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The read is low impact, but sudo/interface ambiguity and automatic driver retries can conceal wrong-path or intermittent SSIF failures.

project_override_considerations: Wistron I2C policy requires the BMC controller/bus and expected response. Here the host command is acceptable only when platform evidence maps its local SSIF transport to FPGA and BMC I2C-1.
expected_evidence: Platform and OS mapping from selected IPMI interface through FPGA to BMC I2C-1 SSIF
Host kernel, ipmitool, driver/module and device-node identities
Pre/post SSIF/I2C/FPGA counters and preserved relevant logs
Timestamped command, stdout/stderr, exit code and duration
Proof no alternate transport/fallback and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source name requires a specific FPGA/I2C-1 SSIF path, while the command does not select or prove its transport and Criteria defines no response fields. DeepSeek/GPT V2 add physical probing that is absent from the source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The functional request and safe command are understood. Missing interface mapping and response oracle are owner-supplied prerequisites, making this RPUC rather than Manual Only or BLOCKED.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row129 Wistron-HW Robust-00007-V003: provide the authoritative mapping from the OS IPMI device/driver through FPGA to BMC I2C-1 SSIF, approved ipmitool interface and sudo policy, expected `bmc info` identity fields, proof that no KCS/BT/LAN/alternate fallback was used, and SSIF/I2C/FPGA timeout/retry/error criteria. Confirm physical probing/photos are not core acceptance unless separately approved.

review_improvement: Changes the physical-only verdict to a gated read-only functional SSIF test and makes path attribution, response content and no-fallback telemetry explicit.
independent_technical_reasoning: `ipmitool bmc info` is a valid application-level request but its success is transport-agnostic unless the OS IPMI device and driver are mapped. The row's unique claim is not merely that the BMC answers; it is that the exchange traverses FPGA and BMC I2C-1 via SSIF. That can be evidenced through interface identity and transport error telemetry without mandatory probing, provided alternate IPMI routes are excluded.
